classification.difficultyReason: Calculate algebraic rectangle areas and subtract an inner area to find each frame's shaded area.

content.prompt: Find the area of each shaded region in terms of $x$.

spec.description: A shaded horizontal rectangle, with 7x cm above its top side and 2x cm beside its right side.
spec.mathematics: Rectangle dimensions 7x cm by 2x cm; the entire rectangle is the requested region.
spec.answerVisibility: Dimensions and shading are permanent givens; no area answer is shown.

spec.description: A shaded square frame surrounding an unshaded square. Both outer dimensions and both inner dimensions are retained.
spec.mathematics: Outer square side 2x cm; inner square side x cm; requested area is outer area minus inner area.
spec.answerVisibility: All four dimension labels and frame shading are permanent givens; no area answer is shown.

answer.short:
$3x^2\text{ cm}^2$

Subtract the inner square's area from the outer square's area.
answer.worked:
Subtract the unshaded inner area from the outer area.

$$\begin{align*}A&=(2x)(2x)-x\times x\\A&=4x^2-x^2\\A&=3x^2\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A shaded horizontal rectangular frame surrounding an unshaded horizontal rectangle. All four dimension labels are retained.
spec.mathematics: Outer rectangle 3x cm by 2x cm; inner rectangle 2x cm by x cm; requested area is their difference.
spec.answerVisibility: Dimensions and frame shading are permanent givens; no area answer is shown.

answer.short:
$4x^2\text{ cm}^2$

Subtract the inner rectangle's area from the outer rectangle's area.
answer.worked:
Subtract the unshaded inner area from the outer area.

$$\begin{align*}A&=(3x)(2x)-(2x)x\\A&=6x^2-2x^2\\A&=4x^2\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
